title: Laminar flow in a straight pipe (the try-out)
summary: Not a validation run: a check that your setup works, before a long run.  The coarsest mesh of the laminar pipe case (Re 100, 5 184 cells) is solved on 2 MPI processes, so every step a real level takes runs once: meshing, gmshToFoam, checkMesh, decomposePar, mpirun, reconstructPar and the clean-up.  The pressure drop it gives is compared with ours.

hexmesh.note: clone this tag with git clone --branch, as in the five commands: the mesh check needs the same meshing code as ours

gmsh.note: the version our meshes were made with; if the mesh check fails, install gmsh 4.12.1

returns: nothing: `collect` writes `poiseuille-try_np2.contrib.json` (about 25 kB) for `check`, and it needn't be sent

try_np2.title: the coarse pipe on 2 processes
try_np2.what: the coarse laminar pipe (5 184 cells), solved by simpleFoam on 2 processes, then collected and checked as a real level is.

reproduce.how: our run on 2 processes (desktop, OpenFOAM v2406 in Docker, 2026-11-22); the same level on 1 process differs by 7e-11 of itself, so 1e-5 leaves room for other platforms and MPI builds, while a wrong mesh or case moves dp by per cent

cores.label: cores (MPI processes)
cores.how: the level is decomposed into 2 slabs along the pipe; prepare --np changes it

wall_time.label: wall time
wall_time.how: prepare 4.6 s, bash job.sh 7.8 s, collect 1.9 s, check about 4 s on the desktop (2026-11-22), once the OpenFOAM image is downloaded; 3 min leaves room for a slower machine

prepare_time.label: time to prepare
prepare_time.how: meshing, gmshToFoam, checkMesh and topoSet: 4.6 s on the desktop (2026-11-22)

peak_memory.label: peak memory
peak_memory.how: a bound: the tool's 2 s sampling saw 0.03 GB over the 6 s solve, too short to measure; 5 184 cells on 2 processes need far less than 1 GB

peak_disk.label: peak disk
peak_disk.how: the run directory after the solve: 1.7 MB (desktop, 2026-11-22); the OpenFOAM image takes about 1.5 GB on the first run
